commitAtDiscovery: uncommitted working tree, branch phase-14-m1-integration (Phase 14 / Milestone M1 DoD verification, in progress)
oneLineDescription: SILENT cross-client divergence — no assertion, no canary, no exception, pendingCount()===0 on all three clients — yet one real client (webkit) ended up with a document that is byte-different from, and 3 characters shorter than, the other two real clients AND the server's own independent operation-log replay. This is the most serious of the four findings: the product's core convergence guarantee actually failed and nothing caught it structurally.
harness: packages/client/_debugNativeRelay60s.mjs, using Playwright's native context.routeWebSocket() + WebSocketRoute.connectToServer() — same harness and same 5-iteration run as R0002/R0003, iteration 0 of 5 (the FIRST iteration of that run).

scenario.markerScheme: one fixed single-character marker per client: chromium=A(client0), firefox=B(client1), webkit=C(client2)
scenario.iterationsResult: iter0 THIS FAILURE, iter1 OK, iter2 CRASH (see R0002), iter3 CRASH (see R0003), iter4 OK (2/5 passed)

diffFindings.client0_vs_serverReplay: byte-identical (0 differences) — i.e. client0 and client1 both match the server's OWN independently-replayed operation log exactly
diffFindings.client0_vs_client2: first differing character at index 98; client2 is a genuinely different, shorter document, not merely a truncation at the end

consoleLogExcerpt: [NATIVE routeWebSocket ~150ms] iter 0 duration=60000ms: MISMATCH len=697 pending=[0,0,0] replayOk=true
notableTimingDetail: UNLIKE R0002/R0003, a real mid-session reconnect DID happen here: replicaId 3 (webkit, the client that ends up diverging) went presence-stale at 11:32:08, came back fresh at 11:32:12, then disconnected (code 1005) and reconnected as a BRAND NEW replicaId 4 at 11:32:13, receiving a fresh SNAPSHOT with lastServerSeq already at 223. The diverging client is exactly the one that reconnected mid-run. This is consistent with (but does not, by itself, prove) a bug in the reconnect/snapshot-reseed path specifically — the fresh Engine seeded from the SNAPSHOT plus whatever the client continued typing afterward apparently lost or misplaced content relative to the server's own ground truth. Combined with R0002/R0003 (canary firures with NO reconnect at all), the current honest state is: there may be TWO distinct real bugs — (a) a reconnect/reseed-path bug producing silent divergence, and (b) a separate, non-reconnect-dependent bug in real concurrent-delivery timing that trips the Case C canary — or one bug reachable through two different paths. Not yet determined; this is exactly what the node-dump root-cause work (packages/client/_debugNodeDump.mjs) is trying to isolate.
reproducibilityCaveat: Same Rule 3 deviation as R0001-R0003: raw operationLog for this occurrence was not persisted before teardown, and worse, the diverging CLIENT's own local operation history was never captured at all (no node-dump hook existed in App.tsx at the time this run happened — that hook was added immediately afterward, specifically in response to this finding). Record is full-fidelity for provenance/pattern-matching (including the actual measured DOM-text divergence and its exact position) but is NOT a byte-exact deterministic reproducer.
status: RESOLVED (test-infrastructure, not product) — see tests/regression/README.md's FINAL RESOLUTION section, 2026-08-31. Confirmed as a defect in the test harness's delay-injection layer, not in SyncClient/gateway.ts/Engine — see R0001/R0002 for the confirming send-vs-receive/direct-path evidence. Still worth noting on its own: this was the one occurrence where no assertion (canary, pendingCount, invariant) caught the failure, which is a property of the injection-layer defect (a whole batch of frames vanishing without a trace on either connection) rather than of anything the product's own safety nets were designed to catch. Entry retained per Rule 2, not removed.
